tts: Excuse me, could you give me some directions, please? — Yes, of course!
Is there a chemist near here? — Yes, there is. It’s in the town centre.
How do I get there? — Go out of the main door and turn left. Then go to the end of the road and turn left again.
Go straight on for about five minutes. Go past the internet café and the bank, and then turn left into Raya Street.

tts: Wow! Look at all this different food! — I know. I can’t decide what I want.
Well, there’s some pizza over there. — No! We can have pizza any day. Let’s try something different.
OK, what about this place? — Mmm, that looks delicious, but what is it? — Excuse me, what is this? — It’s Kung Pao chicken.
It smells so good! What does it come with? — It comes with some noodles.

acts.title: A visitor for the weekend
text: My friend from Poland is here for two days, so I made a plan.
Saturday morning: my neighbourhood. There isn’t much to see — there aren’t any museums — but there’s a good market and a library from 1930.
Then my flat. It’s a studio on the fifth floor, opposite a small park. It isn’t big, but it’s bright and there’s a view of the mountains.
Saturday evening: the Riverside. You need to book online, so I did that on Monday. She’s a vegetarian, so I checked the menu — there are a lot of vegetable dishes.
Sunday: she’s cooking. She says we need a few mushrooms, a little rice and no help from me.

write.q: Put Units 4–6 together: write 8 sentences. Describe your neighbourhood (what there is and isn’t), your home and which floor, the way from the station, what you are wearing today, and what you need to cook dinner — with a quantity.
write.model: In my neighbourhood there’s a library and a lot of cafés, but there aren’t any museums. I live in a flat on the fifth floor, opposite a small park. From the station, go straight on for five minutes and turn left at the traffic lights. It’s the building next to the chemist. Today I’m wearing jeans, because I’m working from home. For dinner I need a little rice, a few mushrooms and some beef. There isn’t enough oil, so don’t forget to buy some.

speak.q: Show a visitor around out loud: say what there is in your area, describe your home, give directions from the station, and then order a meal for two in a restaurant.
speak.model: There’s a market and a library, but there aren’t any museums. I live in a studio flat on the fifth floor, opposite a park. From the station, go straight on and turn left at the lights. — Could I have the grilled fish, please? And can we have some roast potatoes? How much is the set menu?
